lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Match each to its job: parliament; police; court.

FEEDBACK
Parliament makes laws; police enforce laws and keep people safe; courts decide whether a law was broken and what consequence is fair.

WATCH FOR
Thinking the police make the laws mixes up making laws with enforcing them.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw a flow chart showing a law being made, broken, investigated and decided. Write two sentences on why it matters that everyone is treated equally under the law.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Draw a flow chart showing a law being made, broken, investigated and decided. Write two sentences on why it matters that everyone is treated equally under the law. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Example: a driver who is caught speeding gets a fine. For a more serious case, a court with a magistrate or judge listens to both sides and decides. The person is allowed to have a lawyer. Parliament makes the laws, police enforce them and courts decide.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Thinking the police make the laws mixes up making laws with enforcing them. Correction: Parliament makes laws; police enforce laws and keep people safe; courts decide whether a law was broken and what consequence is fair.

Parent: Likely misconception: Thinking the police make the laws mixes up making laws with enforcing them. Keep sample answers out of the child role.
